question.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{3}$ from the denominator, all we need to do is multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{3}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{7}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{7}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{3} & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the product rule to simplify the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{7}\cdot \sqrt{3}}{3} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{7\cdot 3}}{3} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{21}}{3} & \end{aligned}
$$
